finding.get_task: ServerHandler::get_task takes GetTaskParams plus RequestContext<RoleServer> and returns Future<Output=Result<GetTaskResult, McpError>>. The default implementation returns method_not_found, so an application-owned persistent backend can override this method and rehydrate GetTaskResult from its own durable record using the model constructors established in revision 118.
finding.update_task: ServerHandler::update_task takes UpdateTaskParams plus RequestContext<RoleServer> and returns Future<Output=Result<(), McpError>>. The handler does not construct TaskAckResult; the central request dispatcher converts successful unit return with ServerResult::task_ack. This is the minimal source-qualified acknowledgement seam for a persistent backend update.
finding.cancel_task: ServerHandler::cancel_task takes CancelTaskParams plus RequestContext<RoleServer> and returns Future<Output=Result<(), McpError>>. The source documents cancellation as cooperative and explicitly allows observable task status to lag; the central dispatcher converts successful unit return with ServerResult::task_ack.
finding.capability_gate: For tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel, the central Service<RoleServer> dispatcher calls validate_tasks_capability before invoking the override. The server must advertise Tasks and the client must declare Tasks; otherwise the request is rejected before the handler override runs.
finding.adapter_seam: A custom ServerHandler can therefore expose application-owned persistent task state without using stock TaskManager for the three task lifecycle RPCs: get_task reads durable state and returns GetTaskResult; update_task atomically applies accepted inputResponses and returns (); cancel_task records cooperative cancellation intent and returns (). The wire acknowledgement is dispatcher-owned, so no TaskAckResult constructor is required in the custom handler surface.
